Oh boy where do i begin with this...
The bad thing about this game is that, although the story is incredible tragic, which is a good thing in my opinion, fails to deliver consistently. This happens mainly because the story splits into multiple subchapters which will make you lose the plot of the main story. This was kinda frustrating because it ruined my emersion. 
After about 4 hours i gave up on story completly, skipped everything and only played for the insanly good combat and cinematic fights. Which leads me to the verry good thing about this game.. The gameplay or more specific the combat.
The gameplay reminds me verry much of Sekiro, 
Every fight feel more of a dance between you and the boss rather than just a dull hp bar. The parry/deflect/dodge mechanics are verry well implemented in every fight and you will need all 3 of those mechanics in order to beat the game if you play on Legend which i recommend you to. 
The other difficulties gives you a deflect assist button which can make the fights feel more soulless . Like i said, the fights feel more of a choreography rather than just a dull fight and if you enable the assist button will ruin your experience.
The main boss after every chapter will also offer you a solid cinematic experience which im not going to spoil by going into details.

Also, when in character creation, the 'AI' that is supposed to make your character's voice sound like yours doesn't even work. They have certainly lots work to do. After spending an entire weekend exploring the Kaifeng Palace update, I’m completely blown away by the quality and scale of what’s been added. The palace is gorgeous, with intricate architecture, beautiful gardens, and dynamic weather that changes the entire mood of the environment. NPCs have daily routines, meaningful interactions, and unique dialogue that makes the world feel lived-in. The stealth mechanics are tight and satisfying, and sneaking past guards without being detected feels genuinely rewarding. The new boss is challenging, well-animated, and incredibly fun to fight. I also loved the casual activities like ice sculpting and cricket fighting—they’re simple but add so much personality to the game. Best of all, it’s 100% free. The developers have gone above and beyond, and this update cements Where Winds Meet as one of the best wuxia games ever made.

Today i found out that in order to fully replenish your energy, you have to wait 70 hours real time (you burn through energy in no time).

Beautiful graphics, a robust avatar creator, and very engaging stories. I also love the "pet the kitty" mini game.

The good:
- Exploration is fun
- The riddles are fun

The neutral:
- If you squint hard enough the visuals are also quite good
- You can get a lot of stuff for free, so the gamepass mechanics are not that annoying, hope it stays that way
- Controls can be wonky, takes some time to get used to them

The bad:
- Godawful combat. It's not hard, but the level scaling is atrocious, making fighting more than one enemy take SO MUCH time. Hate HP sponges.
- Was the story also written by AI? It's so shallow and the voice acting is so bad I felt like playing someone's poor fanfic
- AI. Yes, it may not be in your face (or is it? it really feels like the whole game was designed by AI) as you would expect, but why are there NPCs serving as chatbots? What is the sense behind it? They are absolutely not interesting, so talking to them feels like a chore. Useless mechanic fueled by useless technology
- You have to switch between single/multiplayer sessions for many of the content and it was starting to get tedious

Overall, I do not recommend. There are so much better titles out there that don't try to be "the best out of all worlds" like this game and failing at almost every aspect.

For the amount of time I've put in so far, it feels like a good game with lots to do. However, I'm not a fan of all of the quick time events (QTE), but thankfully you can set the window for reaction high enough that it doesn't become tedious and frustrating.
There is fishing, which is basic (I'm fine with that as not everything needs to be a complicate minigame), cooking, chess, fighting, exploring, and puzzle aspect (the story has the pieces you need to collect).
As for the performance side, I did not have any issues or bugs so far and it appears to run well on my hardware. Kudos to the dev team, as there are plenty of AAA games that run like crap. AAA games can take a look at this game and see how efficient coding and straight forward games should be done.
